    StartersGotham anniversary popcornPopcorn drizzled with purple and green white chocolateHow to make it100g popcorn kernels200g white chocolate1 drop purple food colouring1 drop green food colouringPop the kernels in a covered pot and split between two trays.Melt the white chocolate, divide in two and tint one half purple and the other green.Drizzle one over each tray and toss. Let set.Break up and mix together in a big bowl.Bat-shaped chips and black bean dipBat shaped fried corn chips with chipotle black bean dipHow to make it10 corn tortillas1 L vegetable oil800g black beans (2 tins), drained2 garlic cloves2 limes1 chipotle in adobosalt, to tasteCut the tortillas with a bat cutter.Fry in the vegetable oil at 180°C in batches until crisp, then salt.Blitz the beans with garlic, lime juice and chipotle until smooth.Serve the dip with the bats.Flugelheim beet-cured salmon on ryeThe Joker's gallery visit, before the paint goes everywhereHow to make itAs written, serves 4Beetroot and gin-cured salmon on rye with horseradish crème fraîche, pickled shallot and a splash of green herb oil, splattered like the gallery.Two days ahead, mix 100g salt, 80g sugar, 1 grated raw beetroot and 2 tbsp gin and pack around a 400g salmon fillet.Cover, weigh down and refrigerate 48 hours, then rinse and slice thin.Blitz a bunch of parsley with 80ml oil and strain.Slice 1 shallot thin and soak in 2 tbsp vinegar.Cut 4 slices rye into 16 squares, spread with crème fraîche mixed with horseradish, top with salmon and shallot, and splash herb oil on the plate.Smoked trout rillettes with toasted briocheVicki at the Flugelheim, before the Joker redecorates.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsManor roast beef and Yorkshire puddingRare rib of beef, roast potatoes, Yorkshire puddings and red wine jusHow to make it2kg beef rib, bone in2 tsp sea salt flakes1kg potatoes100ml vegetable oil3 eggs150g plain flour300ml full cream milk250ml red wine400ml beef stockSalt the beef and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.Roast at 120°C until 52°C inside, then rest.Peel and chop the potatoes and roast them in some of the oil.Whisk the eggs, flour and milk and bake in hot oiled tins at 220°C until puffed.Blast the beef at 260°C for 10 minutes. Reduce the red wine with the stock for a jus.Gotham back-street ReubenThe old-world delis of Gotham's back streetsHow to make itAs written, serves 4Piled-high corned beef, tangy sauerkraut and melted Swiss on rye with house Russian dressing, griddled in butter until crisp, with dill pickles.Mix 4 tbsp mayo, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tbsp horseradish, 1 tbsp chopped pickles and a dash of Worcestershire for Russian dressing.Spread over 8 slices rye.Layer 4 slices with 125g shaved corned beef each, 60g drained sauerkraut and 2 slices Swiss cheese, then close.Butter the outsides and cook in a pan over medium heat with a weight on top for 4 minutes a side until crisp and melted.Halve and serve with pickles.SweetsJoker's birthday cakeChocolate cake with purple and green buttercream and a crooked smileHow to make it450g butter, soft250g caster sugar4 eggs250g self-raising flour50g cocoa200ml full cream milk400g icing sugar1 tsp purple food colouring1 tsp green food colouringHeat the oven to 170°C and prepare two tins. Beat half the butter with the sugar, then beat in the eggs.Fold in the flour, cocoa and milk, divide between the tins and bake.Cool completely.Beat the remaining butter with the icing sugar and tint most purple and a little green.Sandwich and cover the cake, then pipe a crooked smile.DrinksAlfred's Earl Grey gin sourEarl Grey infused gin shaken with lemon, honey and egg whiteHow to make it200ml gin2 Earl Grey tea bags3 tbsp honey2 tbsp hot water3 lemons2 egg whites1 bag iceSteep the tea bags in the gin for an hour, then remove.Dissolve the honey in the hot water. Juice the lemons.Shake the gin, lemon juice, honey syrup and egg whites hard without ice, then add ice and shake again.Strain into chilled coupes and twist lemon peel over each.Kir royaleChampagne and cassis, for the pale moonlight.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
